walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal Assessment: Critical Engagement — a core area of Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Critical Engagement brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Critical Engagement.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: C. Wright Mills published 'The Sociological Imagination' in:

options: Marx
Weber
Comte
Durkheim
Religion is declining in social significance in modern societies.
Religion is becoming more important globally.
A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
Religion has completely disappeared from society.
Strain theory says criminals have psychological strain disorders.
A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
A family formed when partners with children from previous relationships come together — a 'blended' or step-family — one of several family forms recognised in family diversity literature.
A reconstituted family is one that has been put back together after divorce.

mcqs.q: What is Merton's strain theory of crime?
options: A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
Strain theory says criminals have psychological strain disorders.

Crime results from a mismatch between cultural goals (success, wealth) and legitimate means of achieving them — those who can't access legitimate means may innovate (crime), ritualise, retreat or rebel.
Strain theory says people commit crime because they are stressed.
